actionable_steps.citation: From the Mind to the Over-Mind — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 26 (1993), 1993-05-24
actionable_steps.step: Yoke devotion and wisdom together like the pair of bullocks on a cart — let each pull in unison and help the other grow.

actionable_steps.citation: Karma, Upasana and Jnana — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 22 (1989), 1989-10-04
actionable_steps.step: Lay the foundation first: righteous action (karma) and worship (upasana) are the school finals before the degree of jnana.
Seek people who have attained spiritual knowledge — learn their experience, honour them for it, and share their joy with them.
Practise yoga — it is like fire that burns away sins and purifies the inner instrument, and then spiritual wisdom is born there.

actionable_steps.citation: Karma, Upasana and Jnana — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 22 (1989), 1989-10-04
actionable_steps.step: Don't stop at words: make the oneness of the Atma in all a living experience, not a slogan.

definition.citation: Karma, Upasana and Jnana — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 22 (1989), 1989-10-04
definition.quote: Jnana in Vedantic parlance has been defined as "Advaita Darsanam" (recognising the One without a second). That is to see the One in the many.

discourses.citation: Atma Jnana — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 19 (1986), 1986-10-06
discourses.quote: Of all categories of knowledge, the highest is Atma Jnana (the knowledge of the Self). … Worldly knowledge may bring you fame and prosperity. But only Atma Jnana can confer the peace that passeth understanding.

discourses.citation: Total Awareness Is Wisdom — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 26 (1993), 1993-04-12
discourses.quote: You say, "I have read many sacred texts, so I am a great scholar. I am a man of wisdom." … But sacred texts give only minimal knowledge. … This is not full wisdom. This is not full awareness.

discourses.citation: Purity - The Path To Liberation — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 30 (1997), 1997-05-15
discourses.quote: Jnana (Knowledge) does not mean mere acquaintance with books. Nor is it worldly knowledge. Only the person who has recognised the oneness of the Jeevatma (individual spirit) and the Universal Spirit is a real Jnani (one who possesses the supreme wisdom).

make_it_real: Wisdom isn't what you know — it's seeing the One in the many, starting with the person standing in front of you today.
title: Wisdom (Jnana)

vahinis.quote: Light is wisdom. Without light, all is darkness. If you haven't secured the lamp of wisdom (jnana) to illumine your path, you stumble along in the gloom, with fear as your companion.

Yoga gives spiritual wisdom, which confers freedom (moksha) easily. … Yoga is like fire. … It burns away all sins, so the inner instrument (anthah-karana) is rendered pure. When that happens, spiritual wisdom is born there.
